objective: Discharge only the reopened Tool Discovery scope-completeness atom by composing a Brain-owned complete identity gateway, Dynamic V3 finite progress/selection semantics, exact legacy-terminal semantic transport, and the already-separate scope-complete transfer/promotion atoms.

formal_lemmas.statement: Every Brain-invocable tool identity is registered; discovery enumerates exactly the registry; unregistered identities are uninvocable.
The sole owned discovery source is queried at most once per stable epoch and then exposes the exact finite registry.
Each Dynamic V3 PROBE targets one missing required capability on the first non-falsified admissible route; a truthful current-epoch receipt removes that missing pair from the finite progress measure.
Cost/id ordering plus skip-on-false, probe-on-unknown, select-on-all-true makes the first SELECT the least-cost admissible sufficient route under the declared tie-break.
After complete discovery and probe exhaustion, absence of SELECT means every admissible registered route has a truthful negative required-capability witness, so escalation is sound.

Atomic registry replacement increments the universe epoch; both PROBE and SELECT are routed through the owned epoch gate, so stale episodes fail closed before tool interaction. Induction over finite registry changes reduces each episode to T1-T5.
On every valid state of the frozen V1/V2 terminal public schema, Dynamic V3 and the terminal-tested candidate have identical scorer-relevant decision semantics.
Second-task transfer and no-unsupported-promotion remain independently proved scope-complete atoms and are composed later; this scope certificate does not self-credit them.

terminal_evidence_role: The historical 180/180 terminal result is transported to Dynamic V3 as supporting acceptance evidence only; universal scope comes from T1-T6, not empirical extrapolation.
